ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r1.claim: These four verses are God's direct insertion, not Moses's speech; the shift makes the past account address present-day Quraysh and identify their true Lord and rightful object of worship and obedience.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.claim: The insertion informs Quraysh that the message also concerns them and asks them to recognize who deserves worship and obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r2.anchor: to inform the pharaohs of the Quraysh

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r7.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were many, but he persisted in denying God's messengers and guidance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r7.anchor: God showed the Pharaoh signs of all sorts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p43/r8.claim: The signs' details are given in the Torah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.claim: The first-person wording confirms that the inserted verses are God's words, not part of Moses's conversation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p44/r1.anchor: in the first person and hence they are not part of Moses’ conversation

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r7.claim: The announcement that Pharaoh was shown all the signs is addressed by God to Muhammad and supports reading the preceding first-person clause as God's speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r7.anchor: ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها هذا إخبار من الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهذا يدل على أن قوله فأخرجنا إنما هو خطاب له عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r8.claim: Araynā is from visual seeing and takes two objects; 'all Our signs' means the signs Pharaoh had seen, such as the staff, hand, and affliction, not every sign ever shown.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r8.anchor: أريناه آياتنا هي المنقولة من رأى البصرية، ولذلك تعدت إلى اثنين بهمزة النقل وآياتنا ليس عاما إذ لم يره تعالى جميع الآيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r9.claim: Another view takes 'all' as completeness and the possessive as honorific, as though the phrase said signs belonging to Us.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى آيات بكمالها وأضاف الآيات إليه على حسب التشريف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari suggests Moses showed Pharaoh the miracles of other prophets too, but Abu Hayyan finds this far-fetched because receiving a report is not ordinarily called seeing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r10.anchor: وقيل: يكون موسى قد أراه آياته وعدد عليه ما أوتي غيره من الأنبياء من آياتهم ومعجزاتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r11.claim: Another view reads araynā as knowledge rather than sight, since Pharaoh at that time had seen only the staff and shining hand; the signs were the nine miracles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344/r11.anchor: وقيل: أريناه هنا من رؤية القلب لا من رؤية العين، لأنه ما كان أراه في ذلك الوقت إلا العصا واليد البيضاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r1.claim: The signs may be God's signs of oneness displayed in the kingdom of the heavens and earth, in which case seeing is visual.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أراد بالآيات آيات توحيده التي أظهرها لنا في ملكوت السموات والأرض فيكون من رؤية العين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية وأبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya and Abi say Pharaoh's action is his own acquisition, the basis of reward or punishment; the omitted object of denial is apparently the signs, or possibly Moses and his message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية وأبي: يقتضي كسب فرعون وهذا الذي يتعلق به الثواب والعقاب، ومتعلق التكذيب محذوف فالظاهر أنه الآيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r3.claim: One view says Pharaoh denied the signs' divine origin and called them magic; Abu Hayyan rejects confusion as the explanation, since Pharaoh knew they were signs and denied them through oppression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p344#2/r3.anchor: قيل: ويجوز أن يكون أراد وكذب أنها من آيات الله وقال: من سحر، ولهذا قال أجئتنا لتخرجنا من أرضنا بسحرك يا موسى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r6.claim: God made Pharaoh see the signs, or made him know their validity.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r7.claim: “All” may confirm that all categories or individuals were included; the signs may be the known nine miracles granted specifically to Moses, or a listing of miracles given to others as well.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r7.anchor: على أن المراد بآياتنا آيات معهودة وهي الآيات التسع المختصة بموسى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r8.claim: Pharaoh denied Moses out of extreme obstinacy and refused faith and obedience through arrogance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:54-56/r8.anchor: موسى من فرط عناده. { وأبى } الإيمان والطاعة لعتوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r10.claim: The report of Pharaoh’s signs is addressed to Muhammad, supporting the reading that God’s first-person speech begins with fa-akhrajnā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r10.anchor: وقوله تعالى ولقد أريناه إخبار لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن فرعون، وهذا يؤيد أن الكلام من قوله فأخرجنا إنما هو خطاب لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r11.claim: All refers to the signs shown to Pharaoh, not every sign belonging to God; the signs are attributed to the majestic pronoun to honor them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r11.anchor: وقوله كلها عائد على الآيات التي رآها لا أنه رأى كل آية لله، وإنما المعنى أن الله تعالى أراه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r12.claim: The wording wa-abā establishes Pharaoh’s deliberate acquisition of the act, which is the basis for reward and punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p47#3/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وأبى يقتضي تكسب فرعون وهذا هو الذي يتعلق به الثواب والعقاب

NAHHAS:v3p41/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r8.claim: God showed Pharaoh all the signs given to Moses; the point is that Pharaoh saw them directly, not merely through reports.
NAHHAS:v3p41/r8.anchor: المعنى ولقد أرينا فرعون آياتنا التي أعطينا لموسى صلى الله عليه وسلم كلها والفائدة في هذا أن فرعون رأى الآيات كلها عيانا لا خبرا

NAHHAS:v3p41/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p41/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p41/r9.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to believe.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r6.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh may be God's proofs pointing to His oneness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r7.claim: The signs may mean the miracles Moses brought as proof of his prophethood; this does not mean he saw every divine sign.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r7.anchor: المعجزات الدالة على نبوة موسى , يعني التي أتاها موسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r8.claim: The phrase can mean Pharaoh denied the report and refused obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p407/r9.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh rejected the proof and refused to accept it.

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r5.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were identified as flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, blotting, years, staff, and hand.
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r5.anchor: { ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها } يعنى فرعون، الآيات السبع: الطوفان، والجراد، والقمل، والضفادع، والدم، والطمس،

MUQATIL:20:54-56/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r6.claim: Pharaoh denied that the signs came from God and refused to believe them, claiming they were magic.
MUQATIL:20:54-56/r6.anchor: { فكذب } بها، بأنها ليست من الله، عز وجل، { وأبى } [آية: 56] أن يصدق بها، وزعم أنها سحر.

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r8.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were apparently the staff, the hand, and the other signs displayed before his drowning, though not necessarily all at the first encounter.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r8.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالآيات العصا واليد وسائر الآيات التي أراها موسى فرعون أيام دعوته قبل الغرق

TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r9.claim: 'He denied and refused' describes Pharaoh's general pattern of denial and refusal, not merely his response at the beginning of the mission.
TABATABAI:20:49-79#5/r9.anchor: فالمراد جميع الآيات التي أريها وإن لم يؤت بها جميعا في أول الدعوة

TABRISI:20:53-56/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r9.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh are the nine miracles God gave Moses, proofs of his prophethood, not every sign God could create.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r9.anchor: يعني الآيات التسع أي معجزاتنا الدالة على نبوة موسى

TABRISI:20:53-56/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r10.claim: Pharaoh denied all those signs and refused to believe; alternatively, he rejected the proof and refused to accept it.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r10.anchor: { فكذب } بجميع ذلك { وأبى } أن يؤمن به

TABRISI:20:53-56/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:53-56/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:53-56/r11.claim: God does not mean all signs He is capable of or every sign He created, but the signs He gave Moses.
TABRISI:20:53-56/r11.anchor: ولم يرد سبحانه بذلك جميع آياته التي يقدر عليها ولا كل آية خلقها

STUDYQURAN:20:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r1.speaker: JJ, Z
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r1.claim: “All Our signs” refers to the nine signs Moses brought to Pharaoh and his people.
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r1.anchor: Our signs, all of them refers to the nine signs that Moses brought to Pharaoh and his people (JJ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:20:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r2.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to accept the truth.
STUDYQURAN:20:56/r2.anchor: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to accept the truth (Z)

TAB-FULL:v16p88/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r1.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were all the proofs and arguments establishing the truth of the mission entrusted to Moses and Aaron.
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r1.anchor: أرينا فرعون آياتنا، يعني أدلتنا وحججنا على حقيقة ما أرسلنا به رسولينا، موسى وهارون إليه كلها

TAB-FULL:v16p88/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied and refused the truth brought by Moses and Aaron out of arrogance and obstinacy.
TAB-FULL:v16p88/r2.anchor: أن يقبل من موسى وهارون ما جاءا به من عند ربهما من الحق استكبارا وعتوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r1.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were the nine signs whose details were given earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولقد أريناه} يعني فرعون {آياتنا كلها} يعني الآيات التسع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p424#3/r2.claim: Pharaoh treated all the signs as lies, or accused Moses of lying; he refused monotheism and called Moses a magician.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r4.claim: The person shown the signs is Pharaoh, and the signs are the nine miracles.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r4.anchor: يعني: فرعون { آياتنا كلها } الآيات التسع

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r5.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs, claimed they were magic, and refused to submit.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:55-57/r5.anchor: بها، وزعم أنها سحر { وأبى } أن يسلم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r1.claim: The nine signs were the hand, staff, flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, years of famine, and reduced produce, with 7:130 cited.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها} [طه: 56] التسع: يده، وعصاه، والطوفان، والجراد، والقمل، والضفادع، والدم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p264/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to believe.

QASHANI:20:56-57/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:56-57/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:56-57/r1.claim: The signs are proofs that matter can be transcended and that lights exist.
QASHANI:20:56-57/r1.anchor: { أريناه آياتنا } من الحجج والبينات الدالة على التجرد عن المواد ووجود الأنوار

QASHANI:20:56-57/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:56-57/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:56-57/r2.claim: Pharaoh denies and refuses because he is materially bound, cannot perceive immaterial realities, and resists leaving his bodily dwelling; he calls the proof magic through inability to grasp it.
QASHANI:20:56-57/r2.anchor: { فكذب } لكونها مادة { وأبى } القبول لامتناع إدراكها للمجردات وأنكر إزعاجها عن وكرها البدني

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.claim: Israelite presence in Egypt and Moses' effort to lead them back to their homeland created political anxiety for Pharaoh's government and a psychological warfare setting.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r1.anchor: İsrâiloğulları’nın Mısır’daki varlığının ve Hz. Mûsâ tarafından eski yurtlarına götürülmeleri için ortaya konan çabanın Firavun yönetimi nezdinde oluşturduğu siyasî kaygılar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.claim: Because magic deeply affected the masses and had a religious dimension in that society, foregrounding it as the contest could help establish Moses' prophethood and leadership.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r2.anchor: o günün şartları içinde geniş kitleleri derinden etkilemekte olan ve dinî bir hüviyet de taşıyan sihir olgusunu ön plana çıkaran bir mücadele metodu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.claim: Pharaoh and his elite regarded magic as their most effective weapon against monotheism, pressured and rewarded the magicians, and expected an absolute victory.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r3.anchor: sihri tevhid çağrısına karşı kullanabilecekleri en etkili silâh olarak görüyorlar ve sihirbazlara bir taraftan baskı, bir taraftan da teşvik uygulayarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.claim: God equipped Moses with miracles that nullified the magicians' skills, giving Pharaoh and his circle another opportunity to be tested.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r4.anchor: İlâhî irade böyle bir atmosferde Hz. Mûsâ’yı sihirbazların bütün hünerlerini boşa çıkaracak mûcizelerle donatıp Firavun ve çevresindekilere bir imtihan fırsatı daha vermek şeklinde tecelli etmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.claim: The commentary points readers to compare the Qur'anic account with the Biblical account of the episode.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r8.anchor: bu olayla ilgili bilgilerin Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’tekilerle karşılaştırılması için bk. A‘râf 7/103-126

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r9.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r9.claim: Commentators generally take the signs shown to Pharaoh as proofs of God's oneness and miracles demonstrating Moses' prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r9.anchor: Tefsirlerde 56. âyette Firavun’a gösterildiği ifade edilen kanıtların neler olduğu açıklanırken genellikle tevhide

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r10.claim: Although the verse says “all Our signs,” Arabic usage supports understanding it as “many” or “so many of Our signs,” rather than literally every sign.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:56/r10.anchor: Arap dilindeki kullanımlar dikkate alınarak bu ifadenin, “pek çok âyetimizi / kanıtımızı, bunca âyetimizi / kanıtımızı” şeklinde anlaşılmasının uygun olacağı

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p309/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p309/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p309/r1.claim: Al-Jurjānī argues that poets intentionally arrange grammatical relations: Imruʾ al-Qays must know نبك answers the imperative قفا, ذكرى is annexed to حبيب, and منزل is coordinated with it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p309/r1.anchor: أن يكون امرؤ القيس حين قال : ( قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل ) قاله وهو لا يعلم ما نعنيه بقولنا : إن ' قفا ' أمر ، و ' نبك ' جواب الأمر

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r1.claim: أرينا is from visual رأى; the causative hamza gives it two objects, Pharaoh and the signs, so the sense is 'We showed him.'
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r1.anchor: هي من " رأى " البصرية فلما دخلت همزة النقل تعدت بها إلى اثنين أولهما الهاء، والثاني " آياتنا "

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r2.claim: The possessive construction supplies prior definiteness: the familiar signs such as the staff and hand, since Pharaoh did not see all God's signs.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r2.anchor: والإضافة هنا قائمة مقام التعريف العهدي أي: الآيات المعروفة كالعصا واليد ونحوهما، وإلا فلم ير الله تعالى فرعون جميع آياته.

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the signs broadly: Moses showed his mission's signs and recounted earlier messengers' signs, whose reports carry the force of witnessed proof.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r3.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يراد بها الآيات على العموم بمعنى: أن موسى عليه السلام أراه الآيات التي بعث بها وعدد عليه الآيات

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r4.claim: The Sheikh objects that being informed of something is not called seeing except by a remote metaphor.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وفيه بعد؛ لأن الإخبار بالشيء لا يسمى رؤية له إلا بمجاز بعيد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r5.claim: Another view understands seeing as inward cognition, meaning 'We made him know'; its support is that he saw only the hand and staff.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r5.anchor: وقيل: بل الرؤية هنا رؤية قلبية، فالمعنى: أعلمناه " وأيد ذلك: بأنه لم يكن أراه إلا اليد والعصا فقط.

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r6.claim: Those who allow a word to carry literal and figurative senses, or an ambiguous word to carry both, permit both senses here.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r6.anchor: ومن جوز استعمال اللفظ في حقيقته ومجازه أو إعمال المشترك في معنييه يجيز يراد المعنيان جميعا

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r7.claim: The emphasis كلها signals universal scope, removing any suggestion that only a subset of signs was meant; this fits inward sight of signs proving God's oneness and the messenger's truth.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r7.anchor: وتأكيده للآيات ب " كلها " يدل على إرادة العموم لأنهم قالوا: فائدة التوكيد ب " كل " وأخواتها رفع توهم وضع الأخص موضع الأعم،

SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r8.claim: The object of 'denied and refused' is omitted to magnify it, since it is understood.
SAMIN-DURR:20:56/r8.anchor: ولم يذكر معفول التكذيب والإباء تعظيما له، وهو معلوم.

ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n38/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari, Razi and Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n38/r1.claim: Zamakhshari, Razi, and Baydawi read araynahu here as “made him acquainted with” or “made him aware of,” although its literal sense is “We showed him.”
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n38/r1.anchor: According to Zamakhshari, Razi and Baydawi, this verb has here the meaning of "We made him acquainted with" or "aware of".

ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n39/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n39/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n39/r1.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh include both the messages entrusted to Moses and the intangible messages conveyed by God's creation in the preceding passage.
ASAD-NOTES:20:56#n39/r1.anchor: both those entrusted directly to Moses and the intangible "messages" forthcoming from God's creation

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r1.claim: This oath-marked clause briefly recaps what happened between Moses and Pharaoh, emphasizing the importance of the account.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r1.anchor: حكاية أخرى إجمالية لما جرى بين موسى عليه السلام وفرعون عليه اللعنة وتصديرها بالقسم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r2.claim: أرى may derive from visual perception or recognition, each originally taking one object and a second with the causative form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r2.anchor: والأراءة من الرؤية البصرية المتعدية إلى مفعول واحد وقد تعدت إلى ثان بالهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r3.claim: Alusi rejects the knowledge verb analysis because it would require an impermissibly omitted third object in a reporting construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون من الرؤية بمعنى العلم المتعدى إلى اثنين بنفسه وإلى ثالث بالهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r4.claim: Attributing the showing to God’s majestic plural magnifies the signs and Pharaoh’s persistence, and supports reading the preceding relative clause as God’s speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r4.anchor: وإسناد الأراءة إلى ضمير العظمة نظرا إلى الحقيقة لا إلى موسى عليه السلام نظرا إلى الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r5.claim: The account says God showed Pharaoh the staff and hand after Pharaoh demanded proof, matching the earlier narrative of Moses’ signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r5.anchor: حين قال لموسى عليه السلام : ان كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r6.claim: Though there are two signs, Arabic may use the plural for a pair; alternatively, each miracle contains many remarkable details, each a sign.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r6.anchor: من بدائع الأمور التى كل منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r7.claim: A report describes an eighty-cubit terrifying serpent; Pharaoh fled, a crowd crush killed twenty-five thousand, and he begged Moses by God who sent him to remove it, whereupon it became a staff again.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r7.anchor: فانه روى أنه عليه السلام لما ألقاها انقلبت ثعبانا أشعر فاغرافاه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r8.claim: Another report says the serpent rose a mile, swooped toward Pharaoh, and spoke to Moses; Pharaoh pleaded for its removal and it changed back into a staff.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r8.anchor: وروى انها انقلبت حية ارتفعت فى السماء قدر ميل ثم انحطت مقبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r9.claim: Moses’ hand shone with extraordinary luminous whiteness, brighter than the sun and drawing onlookers to marvel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r9.anchor: بياضا نورانيا خارجا عن حدود العادات قد غلب شاعه شعاع الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r10.claim: Since many details were not expressly listed, كلها stresses that Pharaoh saw every implication and detail, leaving no excuse.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r11.claim: Some include the resolution of Moses’ speech impediment among the signs, as they do in God’s command to Moses and Aaron to go with His signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r11.anchor: وأدرج بعضهم فيها حل العقدة كما أدرجه فيها فى قوله تعالى اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r12.claim: A view attributed earlier to Ibn Abbas identifies these signs as Moses’ nine signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r12.anchor: التسع كما روى عن ابن عباس فيما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r13.claim: Alusi objects that most of the nine appeared only after the magicians’ contest, some decades later; some destroyed rather than guided, and others came after Israel escaped.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r13.anchor: وفيه أن أكثرها إنما ظهر على يده عليه السلام بعد ما غلب السحرة على مهل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r14.claim: Others take the possessive broadly to include miracles of all prophets, since Moses’ truthful report of them counts as showing them to Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r14.anchor: وعد آخرون منها الآيات الظاهرة على أيدى الأنبياء عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r15.claim: Alusi objects that other prophets’ signs are not mentioned here and the coming account of magic and counter-challenge makes this reading unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r15.anchor: مما يبعد ذلك جدا وأبعد من ذلك كله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r16.claim: Alusi calls it even more far-fetched to include Moses’ description of God’s deeds proving His exclusive lordship among the signs shown.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r16.anchor: وأبعد من ذلك كله إدراج ما فصله عليه السلام من أفعاله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r17.claim: Another view takes the possessive as covering every kind of miracle, with كلها confirming all kinds were shown.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r17.anchor: وقيل : الإضافة لاستغراق الأنواع وكل تأكيد له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r18.speaker: السخاوى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r18.claim: Al-Sakhawi classifies miracles as creating what was absent, destroying what existed, or changing something while it remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r18.anchor: قال السخاوى : ترجع إلى إيجاد معدوم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r19.claim: Alusi says the staff and hand show these three categories, but questions whether they exhaust miracles and finds the proposal far-fetched even if they do.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r19.anchor: وفي الانحصار نظر ومع الاغماض عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r20.speaker: الكشفية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r20.claim: The Kashfiyya claim the signs were ʿAli shown to Pharaoh on a horse; Alusi calls the claim manifestly false despite their appeal to plural wording in 3:97.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r20.anchor: وزعمت الكشفية أن المراد من الآيات علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أظهره الله تعالى لفرعون راكبا على فرس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r21.claim: The ف marks immediate sequence; the omitted object is the signs or Moses, and Pharaoh denied without hesitation or delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p215#2/r21.anchor: للتعقيب والمفعول محذوف أي فكذب الآيات أو موسى عليه السلام من غير تردد وتأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r1.claim: He refused to accept the signs, truth, faith, or obedience, persisting in refusal to the utmost.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r1.anchor: قبول الآيات أو الحق أو الايمان والطاعة أى امتنع عن ذلك غاية الامتناع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r2.claim: Most take his denial as deliberate rejection and arrogance, best fitting the condemnation; those who read أريناه as making him know the signs must likewise say he knowingly denied them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p216/r2.anchor: عند الأكثرين جحودا واستكبار وهو الأوفق بالذم ومن فسر أرينا بعرفنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r1.claim: The one shown all the signs is Pharaoh, and the signs are the nine given to Moses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {ولقد أريناه} يعني فرعون، {آياتنا كلها} يعني: الآيات التسع التي أعطاها الله موسى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs, claimed they were magic, and refused to submit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p279/r2.anchor: {فكذب} بها وزعم أنها سحر، {وأبى} أن يسلم.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.claim: God had shown Pharaoh the staff, hand, and other signs; all were perceived by eye and heart, and their extraordinary character demonstrates His power over every possible marvel.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r1.anchor: بالعصا واليد وغيرهما مما تقدم من مقتضى عظمتنا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused to send the Israelites; this concise account is more forceful than the fuller enumeration in al-Aʿrāf.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p25#2/r2.anchor: وهذا ابلغ من تعديد ما ذكر في الأعراف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r1.claim: The sentence resumes the Moses–Pharaoh narrative and introduces the ensuing dialogue; it may coordinate with 20:49 after an ellipsis or stand parenthetically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r1.anchor: قصص موسى عليه السلام مع فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r2.claim: The oath lām and qad express amazement at Pharaoh’s tenacity and stress how firmly he persisted in disbelief despite Moses’ many signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الكلام بلام القسم و ( قد ) مستعمل في التعجيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r3.claim: The signs are summarized and generalized here to emphasize Pharaoh’s resistance, unlike al-Aʿrāf, where the aim is to show their succession and support.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r3.anchor: وأجملت وعممت فلم تفصل ، لأن المقصود هنا بيان شدة تصلبه في كفره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r4.claim: God’s showing Pharaoh the signs means making them manifest so that he witnessed them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r4.anchor: وإراءة الله إياه الآيات : إظهارها له بحيث شاهدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r5.claim: The possessive identifies the familiar signs performed through Moses: the staff, white hand, famine years, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, flood, and the sea’s parting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r5.anchor: وهي المذكورة في قوله تعالى : { في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r6.claim: Pharaoh continued denying after all the signs, even entering the parted sea in hope of capturing the Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r6.anchor: وقد استمر تكذيبه بعد جميعها حتى لما رأى انفلاق البحر اقتحمه طمعا للظفر ببني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r7.claim: The emphatic kullah intensifies the audience’s wonder at Pharaoh’s stubbornness; a similar totalizing emphasis appears in the account of Pharaoh’s people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p241/r7.anchor: وتأكيد الآيات بأداة التوكيد { كلها } لزيادة التعجيب من عناده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p243/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p243/r1.speaker: المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p243/r1.claim: Commentators commonly coordinate 20:56 with 20:49 and make 20:49 explain the denial; this wrongly suggests all signs preceded Pharaoh’s summoning magicians, though many came much later. The waw does not require sequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p243/r1.anchor: وظاهر صنيع المفسرين أنهم جعلوا جملة ولقد أريناه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r1.claim: The “him” is Pharaoh, and “all Our signs” means the nine signs, not every sign of God, which cannot be counted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ولقد أريناه يعني فرعون آياتنا كلها يعني التسع الآيات ولم ير كل آية الله لأنها لا تحصى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r2.claim: Pharaoh called the signs magic and refused to believe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p294/r2.anchor: فكذب أي نسب الآيات إلى الكذب وقال هذا سحر وأبى أن يؤمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299#2/r1.claim: The referent is Pharaoh: proofs and signs were established before him and plainly witnessed, yet he rejected them in disbelief, stubbornness, and transgression, as others rejected signs despite inward certainty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p299#2/r1.anchor: يعني: فرعون، أنه قامت عليه الحجج والآيات والدلالات

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r4.anchor: الإباء: الامتناع، أبى يأبى إباء: امتنع

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r9.claim: Kullahā is accusative as an adjective qualifying āyāt.
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r9.anchor: ويحتمل الجر على تقدير: ويوم يحشر الناس كلها نصب نعت للآيات

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r10.claim: God showed Pharaoh every proof given to Moses and other evidence as well.
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r10.anchor: أي: أرينا فرعون كل الأدلة التي أعطيناها موسى وغير ذلك

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r11.claim: Abu Muslim identifies the signs as proofs of monotheism and justice and guidance for those seeking guidance.
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو أدلة التوحيد والعدل وما يهدي به المهتدي، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r12.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r12.claim: Abu Ali identifies them as Moses' miracles proving God's unity and Moses' prophethood; God attributes them to Himself because Moses displayed them by His power.
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r12.anchor: التي أعطيناها موسى الدالة على توحيد الله تعالى ونبوة موسى، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v7p4680/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r13.claim: After seeing the signs, Pharaoh called Moses a liar and refused the call to worship and obey God; he then accused Moses of sorcery to mislead his people.
JISHUMI:v7p4680/r13.anchor: فكذب موسى بعد رؤية الآيات أي: وصفه بالكذب وأبى وامتنع عن قبول ما دعي إليه من توحيد الله تعالى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r1.claim: The nine signs were staff, hand, sea split, stone, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, and uprooting the mountain.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r1.anchor: وهي تسع آيات العصا واليد وفلق البحر والحجر والجراد والقمل والضفادع والدم ونتق الجبل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p58#2/r2.claim: Pharaoh denied the signs and refused the truth.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r1.claim: The signs shown to Pharaoh were miracles proving Moses' prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولقد أريناه آياتنا كلها } أي المعجزات الدالة على نبوة موسى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r2.claim: Another view takes the signs as God's proofs of His oneness.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r2.anchor: وقيل: حجج الله الدالة على توحيده.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r3.claim: Pharaoh refused to believe; his denial was obstinate because he saw the signs directly rather than hearing about them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r3.anchor: { فكذب وأبى } أي لم يؤمن. وهذا يدل على أنه كفر عنادا، لأنه رأى الآيات عيانا لا خبرا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r4.claim: Qurṭubī compares this with those who inwardly knew truth but rejected signs unjustly and arrogantly.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:56-58/r4.anchor: نظيره وجحدوا بها واستيقنتها أنفسهم ظلما وعلوا

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r3.claim: The definite form of signs refers to the known signs, while kulluhā confirms that every kind was included.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r3.anchor: إضافة الآيات عهدية وكلها تأكيد لشمول الأنواع

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r4.claim: Through Moses God showed Pharaoh all the signs, including the staff and the hand, over time; alternatively He made their truth known and clarified their evidentiary force.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r4.anchor: أي : وبالله لقد بصرنا فرعون على يدي موسى آياتنا كلها

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r5.claim: Pharaoh denied all the signs from obstinacy, without pause or hesitation, and claimed they were magic.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r5.anchor: {فكذب} بالآيات كلها من فرط عناده من غير تردد وتأخير

BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r6.claim: Ibāʾ is intense refusal: every case of ibāʾ is refusal, but not every refusal is ibāʾ.
BURSEVI:v5p305#2/r6.anchor: والاباء شدة الامتناع فكل اباء امتناع وليس كل امتناع إباء
